headline: China's memory chipmaker CXMT estimates its third-quarter revenue at about seven times last year's, as AI demand lifts memory prices.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: company-reported figures from 16 Oct, large enough to matter to memory buyers, but preliminary.
importance_line: It shows how the AI-driven memory shortage is lifting a Chinese challenger to Samsung and SK hynix, which matters to memory buyers and rival makers, but the figures are the company's own preliminary estimates.
source: Seoul Economic Daily, citing Star Market Daily and Yicai
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports, citing Star Market Daily and Yicai, that CXMT, a Chinese maker of DRAM memory chips that competes with Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, estimated in a preliminary earnings notice on 16 Oct 2026 that third-quarter revenue will be 114.7 billion to 119.7 billion yuan, up 589 to 619 percent from a year earlier, and that its net profit for the first nine months will be 131 billion to 132.5 billion yuan against a loss of 5.3 billion yuan a year earlier. CXMT said demand for AI computing power rose faster than supply and pushed memory prices up sharply, and its chairman, Zhu Yiming, proposed a share buyback of 1 billion to 2 billion yuan.
notes: Full text read. Seoul Economic Daily relays Star Market Daily and Yicai (AI-translated from Korean); the figures are the company's unaudited preliminary range.
